classification.difficultyReason: Choose a general linear remainder and use the two supplied remainder values at the quadratic divisor's roots to determine its coefficients.

content.prompt: When $P(x)$ is divided by $x+2$ and $x-3$, the remainders are $-11$ and $9$ respectively. Find the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $x^2-x-6$.

answer.short:
$4x-3$

Write the remainder as $Ax+B$ and use $P(-2)=-11$ and $P(3)=9$.
answer.worked:
The remainder theorem gives $P(-2)=-11$ and $P(3)=9$. Since $x^2-x-6=(x+2)(x-3)$, write
$$P(x)=(x+2)(x-3)Q(x)+Ax+B.$$
Substituting the roots of the divisor gives
$$\begin{align*}
P(-2)&=-2A+B=-11\\
P(3)&=3A+B=9.
\end{align*}$$
Subtract the first equation from the second:
$$\begin{align*}
5A&=20\\
A&=4\\
B&=9-3(4)\\
B&=-3.
\end{align*}$$
Hence the remainder is $4x-3$.
